title: Commands of a -man dashboard (gitman, dcman, checkman)
description: <config dir>/<app>/commands.yaml. Each command gets a palette entry, a key when it is free, and runs a shell line with the selection filled in.

id.description: Unique; the favorites file stores it.

key.description: Optional. One character (z, Z, ?), ctrl+<letter>, alt+<character> or a named key (f1–f12, home, end, pgup, …); Ctrl+G is read as ctrl+g. Refused: ctrl+c (always quits), ctrl+i/m/[ (the terminal sends them as tab, enter, esc), ctrl+s/q (flow control), ctrl+b (tmux prefix), and any key a built-in command already has in the view, which leaves the command palette only.

label.description: Shown in the palette and the footer.

view.description: Where it works: all, or a view of the app. gitman: log, status, branches. dcman: summary, logs, stats, env, ports, inspect, compose, output. checkman: results, environments, spec, history.

run.description: Shell line. {name} placeholders are filled with shell-quoted values; do not quote them. gitman: {hash} {short} {branch} {current} {file} {base} {repo}. dcman: {service} {container} {project} {file}. checkman: {env} {place} {key} {spec} {report}. All: {input}, the answer to ask.

ask.description: Question asked first; the answer fills {input}.

terminal.description: Hand over the terminal, for interactive commands such as git add -p.
